## Summary
Lenses checked: correctness, silent-failure, tests, comments.
The `--wait` alias that ADR 007 promises is missing, so existing scripts that pass `--wait` fail as soon as this change ships. That alias needs to be restored before merge.

## Changes
The pull request renames the CLI option `--wait` to `--timeout` in `app/cli.py` and updates the tests to match. It also adds ADR 007 on the terminology change and a root-level `review.txt`.

## Critical
- app/cli.py:6 — correctness — Restore `--wait` as a deprecated alias for `--timeout` — `parse_args(["--wait", "12"])` now exits with code 2 ("unrecognized arguments") because `--wait` is no longer registered. `docs/adr/007-timeout.md:5` states "Accept `--wait` as an alias for one release and emit a deprecation warning when it is used," and no code or test does this. — Every existing script or invocation that uses `--wait` breaks without the deprecation period the ADR promises. — Fix: Register `--wait` with `dest="timeout"` and a custom action that emits a `DeprecationWarning`, then add a `--wait` case to `test_explicit_options` that asserts the warning.
